sessions.text:
User: Quick request first: tag every Terraform resource you write with Owner = "data-team".
Assistant: Sure, every Terraform resource gets the Owner tag set to data-team. What else should I know?
User: I default to eu-central-1 for AWS deployments.
Assistant: Noted, eu-central-1 is your default AWS region.
User: Thanks. Unrelated: is Terraform's S3 backend still the usual way to store state?

User: Project Wren needs its first AWS environment this week. It's a batch job that renders thumbnails for uploaded photos.
Assistant: Understood. Are the uploads already stored somewhere, or does that need setting up too?
User: They land in an existing bucket owned by the mobile team, we just read from it.
Assistant: Then the main new pieces are the compute and the output bucket. Where will the users be?
User: For Project Wren, deploy to us-west-2. Most of the mobile users are in California.
Assistant: us-west-2 for Project Wren, noted. I'll draft the compute stack there.

User: More on Project Wren. The thumbnail job is taking about 4 seconds per photo.
Assistant: That's slow for thumbnails. Are the photos large originals?
User: Yes, most are 12 megapixel, some bigger.
Assistant: Downscaling during decode instead of resizing after a full decode usually helps a lot at that size.
User: Good tip, I'll try that. How many free Lambda requests do we get per month?
Assistant: The free tier includes one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds of compute per month, though it can change, so check the pricing page.
User: Right. Actually, for Project Wren, switch to ap-northeast-1 for deployments. Our main customers have moved to Tokyo.
